title: Number Magic
story: You pull out a napkin at lunch and tell your friends: 'Pick any number, and I'll guess the answer — it's always 5!' They're amazed when it works every time.
why: Following the steps of an algorithm with variables shows how math operations chain together to produce consistent results.
analogy: A magic trick is just following a recipe with surprise at the end — your program reveals every step so the audience can see there's no cheating.
try_it: Try different starting numbers: 7, 13, 100, 999. The result is always 5! Can you figure out why mathematically?
tips: Use descriptive variable names like `doubled` and `plus_ten` so each step is self-explanatory
Print each intermediate step so you can watch the magic unfold in the output
The trick works because the math simplifies: the original number cancels itself out
common_mistakes: Doing all the math in one line — splitting it into steps makes it easier to understand and debug
Forgetting that Int division drops decimals — `11 / 2` gives `5`, not `5.5`
